R134.note: AddParameter passes serverName as data and closes the injection, but the response body changes from powershell.exe's formatted stdout to PSObject.ToString() (type names for PS7 PingStatus objects), a catch-all now maps every failure to 400, and a new Microsoft.PowerShell.SDK dependency is required - none of which the write-up states.

R135.note: toRealPath() on both sides plus Path.startsWith rejects absolute and traversal inputs before readAllBytes; nonexistent files still surface as NoSuchFileException as before, matching the stated contract.

R136.note: bin2hex(random_bytes(16)) replaces uniqid and the attacker-controlled prefix; the 32-hex-char token format is stated in the write-up.

R137.note: Positional ? parameter with the %..% pattern supplied as the bound value preserves the original LIKE semantics; AddWithValue's name is ignored by ODBC so binding works.

R138.note: html.EscapeString on both fields at the sink; the local html variable only shadows the package after the declaration so the call resolves to the package (Build OK confirms).

R139.note: Generic 'Invalid order ID' body with the same 400 status; exception message no longer reaches the client.

R140.note: EJS <%= %> auto-escapes and closes the XSS, but the fix adds a runtime dependency on the ejs package that the write-up wrongly claims ships with Express - if it is not installed res.render fails for every request.

R141.note: @csrf_protect added in the same decorator order as the sibling route; only the now-stale docstring still claims the decorator is missing.

R142.note: RandomNumberGenerator fills the 16 bytes and the Base64 response shape is unchanged; the unused seed parameter is left in the signature, which is harmless.

R143.note: Build FAIL: the controller does not extend a base with AuthorizesRequests so $this->authorize() is undefined and every request, including an authorized one, fatals before refund() - the write-up does not say the trait/base class must be added.

R144.note: The character allowlist keeps cmd metacharacters out of the /C line but leaves the shell-string shape and leading-hyphen option injection (e.g. target=-t makes ping run indefinitely) instead of separate exec.Command argument arrays; it also rejects IPv6 targets while the write-up claims legitimate IPs pass unchanged.

R145.note: Allowlist mapping is the right shape for import_module, but it silently rewrites the module path from csv_export to plugins.csv_export (the docstring describes plugins as plain importable modules) and limits the endpoint to two hard-coded plugins without flagging either as an assumption to adjust.

R146.note: jwt.verify with a pinned HS256 allowlist and env secret closes the forgery; the 500-on-missing-secret and HS256 assumption are both stated plainly.
